# Independent audit: cap-plus-section nonlogconcavity below OC

Source: `candidate e882d86157f45ea0`.
I read and ran `supporting computation verify_cap_plus_section_nonlogconcavity.py`.
**PASS**, including every displayed rational constant.

The product `[-1,1] x K` is a full-dimensional convex body with exactly
three integer fibers, each the standard five-simplex of volume `1/120`.
Thus the intrinsic measure is `H_5`, equal to the fiber-volume sum, and
the total is `1/40`. The cap's continuous normal is already unit length.
Its three coordinate thresholds are strictly between zero and one,
so every cut is proper and has no fiber boundary mass.

At threshold `x_1=1-t`, direct simplex slicing gives cap volume
`(1-t^5)/120` and Euclidean section measure `t^4/24`. There is no
additional coarea or oblique-normal factor. The normalized cap mass is
exactly `1406574933/10000000000`, below `gamma_5/2` by
`146483541281/2430000000000`.

For the prescribed coefficient one half, the common-rescaled weight is
`h(t)=1-t^5+(5/2)t^4`. Direct expansion verifies

`h h''-(h')^2=5t^2(1-t)(1+t)((t-1)^4+5)>0`

throughout `0<t<1`. The sampled log-concavity deficit is the positive
rational value in (4). Moreover the displayed second-derivative formula
for every positive power of `h` is correct, so no positive-power
concavity can hold on this sampled triple either.

The conclusion is specifically a structural counterexample for actual
cap-plus-full-section weights with a prescribed nonnegative coefficient.
The note does not assert that this coefficient occurs in an attained
normal stress or that the cap belongs to a below-OC full cover. Thus it
does not furnish an OC counterexample or rule out an additional
restriction obtainable from genuine optimizing stresses.
